mike: Heads up — FlashAttention upstream changed the vec4 path (fa/v2) and our kernel selector is preferring it. Seeing ~2.3x memory spikes and KV-cache thrash on long-chat workloads. PR: https://github.com/flash-attention/flash-attention/pull/1234 commit abcdef1 :eyes:

tara: Copy. Do you have a short repro? Which model, seq len, batch?

mike: Repro: llama-13b, seq=4096, batch=4, staged-paged-kv enabled. Local bench command: 
```bash
./tools/bench_attention --model llama-13b --seq-len 4096 --batch 4 --use-paged-kv --backend flashattn
```
Gists with perf traces: https://git.redwood/internal/trace/1799

ben: CI perf runs (nightly) also show regressions when vendorPinned->fa@abcdef1. Quick snapshot from perf dashboard: 
```
config         | latency(ms) | throughput(tok/s)
------------------------------------------
baseline (fa@abcdef0) | 48          | 120k
fa@abcdef1            | 70          | 74k
xformers-fallback     | 65          | 80k
```

dave: Is this the vec4 alignment rewrite we saw in vendor patch last month? That one changed pad_to_multiple_of_16 -> pad_to_multiple_of_32 in a few hot paths, could interact with our page rounding.

build-bot: CI job #1976: perf/regression/flashattn — FAILURE. latency +45%, throughput -38%. Full log: https://ci.redwood/jobs/1976/log

tara: Quick profiler snapshot (heap allocations): extra transient buffer allocations in flash_attn::prepare_qkv when vec4 path triggers. Suspect the code path uses a temporaries-for-alignment trick. Patch idea: guard vec4 route behind runtime alignment check + opt-out env flag.

mike: Proposed quick mitigation: selector override env REDWOOD_FA_DISABLE_VEC4=1 so we force older vector path until upstream stabilizes. Plan to canary deploy to Dedicated for a few customers.

ben: Also please vendor-pinning note: we should revert to fa@abcdef0 in our submodule and cut a short-lived release. Add a unit test that exercises KV page wrap (seq boundary + small pages).

dave: Also add a Console metric: inference.kv.cache_page_evictions and alert on >10% increase vs baseline in last 6h. That will catch regressions we missed.

tara: I'll open eng-runtime PR: branch fix/fa-vec4-guard. Will include: env toggle, CI perf job, micro-bench pre/post. ETA EOD.

mike: Thanks. tagging @oncall for weekend watch /cc dave :thumbsup:

ben: FYI — vendor team flagged a downstream vendor drop that also includes a different alignment change. Coordinating with them to avoid two simultaneous alignment rewrites.

dave: If we need a hotfix immediately, we can ship runtime patch that short-circuits selector when "paged_kv_enabled && seq_len >= 2048". Safer than global opt-out.

mike: Agree. Tara + Ben please coordinate on test matrix. I'll create a canary config and schedule the deploy window.

build-bot: Noted: job created #1980 for canary perf run.

tara: Uploading initial perf numbers to the PR in a bit, will include perf/heap snapshots and flamegraphs.

mike: Great — keep this thread updated. If anyone reproduces different behavior on ampere vs h100, call it out explicitly.
